subject: TS-6 C2 release verifier wired into CI, plus the provenance audit the owner required before any commit
instruction: No commit, push or PR. This entry prepares the exact changeset boundary so the owner can authorise a commit without the two workstreams silently merging.

part1_releaseVerifier.ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml — quality job, immediately after the Typecheck step: `run: npm run verify:ts6-c2`
part1_releaseVerifier.whyItIsADeterministicGateNotAHardcodedNu: It never asserts `96 / 17`. It RE-DERIVES the authority through buildAuditShape and resolveReachability, then checks that the committed golden.v6 still follows from it. A drift in the authority fails the gate until the lineage is deliberately re-derived.
checks: 1. frozen artifacts preserved — sha256 of frozen v2, crosswalk and golden.v5 must be byte-identical
2. current authority inventory — 120 candidates / 113 boundaries / 11 raw sites, counted independently of status
3. current authority classification — REVIEW_REQUIRED must be 0, TX_BOUNDARY + TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD must reconcile to 113, and every PROVEN boundary must carry a qualified caller

4. golden.v6 lineage — validateCorpus must return valid=true with 0 issues against the CURRENT authority (this is the 'the committed classification still follows from the committed authority' claim), summary must equal the re-derived classification, one row per boundary
5. relation graph — 112 declared relations, every covers[] target back-referenced, every PROVEN row carrying a resolving relation, lineage PROVEN count equal to the derived count

6. legacy authority retirement — the legacy reconstruction is still reachable for historical assertions, the two authorities must DIFFER (proving the replacement is actually in effect), and the inventory must not move with the authority

negativeTest.method: flipped one PROVEN boundary to TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD inside golden.v6 only, decrementing the summary, then re-ran the gate
negativeTest.result: exit 1 with 3 FAILs — 'golden.v6 validates clean against the current authority' (REACHABILITY_DRIFT, SUMMARY_COUNT x2), 'golden.v6 summary is the re-derived classification' (v6 95/18/0 != derived 96/17/0), 'lineage PROVEN count equals the derived classification' (95 != 96)
negativeTest.conclusion: the gate genuinely detects lineage drift; it is not a no-op assertion

part1_releaseVerifier.scopeLimitation: This is the ONLY TS-6 C2 enforcement added. The 37-case audit suites (scripts/ts6-audit/*.test.ts) are deliberately NOT added as permanent unit/contract gates — they keep their teardown defect and their issue-scoped role. Nothing about test:contract, Stage 9, NetworkX or the timeouts was changed.

part2_provenanceAudit.why: The owner required a check that the dirty worktree's other production changes cannot ride along in the TS-6 commit. 'Looks unrelated' is not the same claim as 'is not in the commit'.
part2_provenanceAudit.finding: The worktree is NOT one changeset. It carries TWO workstreams, and the production changes are real functional work — not formatting or incidental noise.

evidence: 12 added lines across the production diff reference OUTCOME_UNKNOWN / outcome-state handling
sample: modules/discovery-runtime/src/worker.ts adds `isOutcomeUnknown()` and a `preserveLeaseForRecovery` path that keeps the lease fence alive on OUTCOME_UNKNOWN
the two ADRs and the TS-6 transaction-outcome tests are dirty together, which is the OUTCOME_UNKNOWN workstream
otherUnrelatedGroupsAlsoDirty: package.json was ALREADY modified before this round (the pre-existing R12 `test:unit --maxWorkers=2`)

theBoundaryIsCleanerThanItFirstLooked.whatIsStillNeededFromTheOwner: a decision on whether the two workstreams land as separate commits/PRs or as one declared PR. That is a governance call, not derivable from the code.

B. land them as one declared PR, explicitly stating that it contains both, so the review and the CI result cover the real head
